title: Solutions
summary: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances; the component present in larger amount is the solvent and the other the solute. Solutions may be gaseous, liquid or solid. Concentration terms: mass per cent (w/w), volume per cent, mole fraction x = n_A/(n_A + n_B) (sum of mole fractions is 1), molarity M = moles of solute per litre of solution, molality m = moles of solute per kg of solvent, normality. Molarity changes with temperature while molality and mole fraction do not. Solubility of a gas in a liquid increases with pressure (Henry's law: p = K_H · x) and decreases with rise of temperature.

Vapour pressure is the pressure of the vapour in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature; it increases with temperature, and the boiling point is the temperature at which the vapour pressure equals the external pressure. Raoult's law: the partial vapour pressure of a component in a solution is p_A = x_A · p°_A; for a solution of a non-volatile solute the relative lowering of vapour pressure equals the mole fraction of the solute: (p° − p)/p° = x_B = n_B/(n_A + n_B). Ideal solutions obey Raoult's law at all concentrations (ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0; e.g. benzene + toluene, hexane + heptane). Non-ideal solutions show positive deviation (weaker A–B attraction: ethanol + acetone, ΔH > 0) or negative deviation (stronger A–B attraction: chloroform + acetone, HNO3 + water, ΔH < 0); they form azeotropes.

Properties that depend only on the number of solute particles are colligative: relative lowering of vapour pressure, elevation of boiling point ΔT_b = K_b·m, depression of freezing point ΔT_f = K_f·m, and osmotic pressure π = CRT. Molar mass M_B = (K·w_B·1000)/(ΔT·w_A) for boiling/freezing and M_B = w_B RT/(π V) for osmotic pressure. Osmosis is the flow of solvent through a semipermeable membrane from dilute to concentrated solution; solutions with the same osmotic pressure are isotonic; reverse osmosis (pressure larger than π) is used in desalination. Abnormal molar mass: for electrolytes that dissociate (KCl, K2SO4) or solutes that associate (acetic acid in benzene), the van't Hoff factor i = observed colligative property / calculated value = normal molar mass / observed molar mass; the colligative equations become ΔT_b = i·K_b·m, π = i·CRT. i for NaCl is about 2, K2SO4 about 3 and glucose 1.

objective: State true or false: (a) Raoult's law is applicable only if the liquids are volatile and miscible. (b) The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which its vapour pressure becomes zero.
(a) True. (b) False – it is the temperature at which the vapour pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure.
(a) What is the van't Hoff factor of K2SO4? (b) Write the expression for the elevation of boiling point of an electrolyte using it.
Fill in: (a) The molar concentration of solute particles is related to osmotic pressure by π = ______. (b) A solution with positive deviation has ΔH_mix ______ than zero.
Match: (a) ΔT_b (b) π (c) Henry's law with (i) CRT (ii) K_b·m (iii) gas solubility.
(a) Moles of solute dissolved per litre of solution. (b) Moles of solute dissolved per kilogram of solvent.
Name the type of deviation shown by (a) ethanol–acetone mixture (b) chloroform–acetone mixture.
State true or false: (a) Ideal solutions have ΔV_mix = 0. (b) Reverse osmosis uses pressure smaller than the osmotic pressure.
(a) True. (b) False – larger than the osmotic pressure.

vsa: State Raoult's law for a solution of a volatile liquid.
The partial vapour pressure of each component in a solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction: p_A = x_A · p°_A; the total pressure is the sum of the partial pressures.
April 2026
Calculate the van't Hoff factor of K2SO4 if it dissociates completely, and explain its meaning.
K2SO4 → 2K+ + SO4^2−, so i = 3. It is the ratio of the observed colligative property (number of particles) to the value calculated assuming no dissociation or association.
April 2026
What are non-ideal solutions? Which pair of liquids shows positive deviation?
Solutions that do not obey Raoult's law over the whole range of concentration (ΔH_mix and ΔV_mix are not zero). Ethanol + acetone shows positive deviation.
April 2025
What are colligative properties? Name any two.

Properties of dilute solutions that depend on the number of solute particles and not on their nature, for example relative lowering of vapour pressure and osmotic pressure (also boiling point elevation and freezing point depression).
April 2025
What is osmotic pressure? Write its expression.
The excess pressure that must be applied to the solution side to stop osmosis of the solvent through a semipermeable membrane. π = CRT.
October 2024
What is meant by relative lowering of vapour pressure? Write the relation with mole fraction.
(p° − p)/p° is the relative lowering of vapour pressure; it equals the mole fraction of the non-volatile solute, x_B.
Why does the freezing point of a solvent decrease on adding a non-volatile solute?
The vapour pressure of the solution is lower than that of the pure solvent, so the solution's vapour pressure curve meets that of the solid solvent at a lower temperature.
State Henry's law and give one application.

At constant temperature the solubility of a gas in a liquid is proportional to the pressure of the gas above the liquid (p = K_H·x). Application: soda water is bottled under high CO2 pressure; scuba divers use diluted air to avoid bends.
sa: A solution containing 12.5 g of a non-electrolyte in 175 g of water gave a boiling point elevation of 0.70 K. Calculate the molar mass of the solute (K_b for water = 0.52 K kg mol^-1).
Calculate the molar mass of K2SO4 if a solution of 2.5 g of it in 100 mL has an osmotic pressure of 10.6 atm at 300 K, assuming complete dissociation (R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1).

With complete dissociation i = 3 and π = i (w/M)(RT/V).
M = i w R T / (π V) = 3 × 2.5 × 0.0821 × 300 / (10.6 × 0.1)
= 184.7 / 1.06 = 174 g mol^-1.
Differentiate between ideal and non-ideal solutions (three points) with examples.

Ideal: obey Raoult's law at all concentrations, ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0 (benzene + toluene). Non-ideal: deviate from Raoult's law, ΔH_mix and ΔV_mix non-zero; positive deviation (ethanol + acetone, A–B attraction weaker) or negative deviation (chloroform + acetone, A–B attraction stronger).
What is the molar concentration of solute particles in human blood if the osmotic pressure is 7.2 atm at 37 °C? (R = 0.0821 L atm K^-1 mol^-1)
What is abnormal molar mass? Explain with association and dissociation.

Molar mass determined from colligative properties that differs from the normal value because the solute dissociates (observed molar mass lower, i > 1; KCl in water) or associates (observed molar mass higher, i < 1; ethanoic acid dimerises in benzene). i = normal molar mass / observed molar mass.
Explain osmosis and reverse osmosis with a use of each.

Osmosis: net flow of solvent from dilute to concentrated solution through a semipermeable membrane (swelling of raisins in water). Reverse osmosis: applying pressure greater than the osmotic pressure on the concentrated side pushes solvent out of it; used for desalination of sea water.
la: (a) What are non-ideal solutions? (b) What type of liquid pair shows (i) positive deviation (ii) negative deviation from Raoult's law?

(a) Solutions which do not obey Raoult's law over the entire range of composition; their enthalpy and volume of mixing are not zero.
(b) (i) Positive deviation: when A–B interactions are weaker than A–A and B–B (ethanol + acetone; ΔH_mix > 0, vapour pressure higher than expected). (ii) Negative deviation: when A–B interactions are stronger (chloroform + acetone, HNO3 + water; ΔH_mix < 0, vapour pressure lower than expected).
Define colligative properties and draw (describe) the vapour pressure–temperature curves showing elevation of boiling point.

Colligative properties depend on the number of solute particles in a solution and not on their nature (lowering of vapour pressure, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point, osmotic pressure).
The vapour pressure curve of the solution lies below that of the pure solvent; it reaches 1 atm at a higher temperature, so the boiling point rises by ΔT_b = T_b − T°_b = K_b·m.

(a) State Raoult's law and derive the relative lowering of vapour pressure. (b) The vapour pressure of pure water at 298 K is 23.8 mm Hg; find the vapour pressure when 18 g of glucose is dissolved in 90 g of water.

(a) p_A = x_A p°_A; for a non-volatile solute x_A = 1 − x_B, so p = (1 − x_B)p°, hence (p° − p)/p° = x_B.
(b) n(glucose) = 18/180 = 0.1; n(water) = 90/18 = 5; x(water) = 5/5.1 = 0.980.
p = 0.980 × 23.8 = 23.3 mm Hg.
Explain the van't Hoff factor. How does it modify (a) ΔT_b and (b) π? Calculate the freezing point depression of 0.1 m NaCl solution assuming complete dissociation (K_f = 1.86 K kg mol^-1).

i = observed colligative property / calculated value = normal molar mass / observed molar mass.
(a) ΔT_b = i·K_b·m. (b) π = i·CRT.
For NaCl i = 2: ΔT_f = 2 × 1.86 × 0.1 = 0.372 K.
